title: Happy path - clean PDF, explicit PO, exact match
scenario: Machine-readable PDF, itemised, GST shown separately, PO reference printed. Everything lines up.

title: Bundled line, GST embedded in the total
scenario: One lump-sum line, no subtotal or tax breakdown. The engine must back out 18% GST to compare against the PO's net value.

title: PO reference implied, not stated
scenario: No PO number anywhere. The engine must infer the PO from vendor + amount + description and say how confident it is.

title: Split PO - invoice 1 of 2 (60%)
scenario: Vendor bills 60% of a PO. Approved as a partial; the PO ledger records the balance.

title: Split PO - invoice 2 of 2 (closes the PO)
scenario: The remaining 40%. Cumulative billing now equals the PO exactly, so it is approved and the PO closes.

title: Split PO - a third invoice pushes billing past the PO
scenario: Each invoice looks fine alone; cumulative billing is 108% of the PO. Only the cumulative ledger catches it.

title: Near-miss amount - 1.2% over PO, inside tolerance
scenario: Net 80,960 vs PO 80,000. Not exact, but within the 2% tolerance - approved with the variance recorded.

title: Near-miss amount - 6% over PO, outside tolerance
scenario: Net 53,000 vs PO 50,000. Close enough to look right, too far to pay without a person looking.

title: Duplicate - the same invoice sent again
scenario: Same vendor and invoice number as scenario 01, but a different file (a 'reminder' copy). Must not be paid twice.

title: Missing invoice number + looks like a duplicate
scenario: No invoice number at all, but vendor, date and amount match scenario 02. Can't be proven a duplicate, can't be safely paid.

title: Vendor not on the approved list
scenario: Valid-looking invoice from a supplier procurement has never onboarded. Held and routed to vendor onboarding.

title: Scanned image - no text layer, all fields present
scenario: Image-only PDF with skew and noise. Needs OCR / vision to read. Once read, it is a clean match.

title: Scanned image - invoice date missing
scenario: Scan with no invoice date. The engine must not guess: it holds and drafts a query to the vendor.

title: Lines don't add up to the stated subtotal
scenario: Line items sum to 74,500 but the subtotal says 75,500 (+Rs 1,000). The stated total is within PO tolerance - only the arithmetic check catches it.
